acceptance_criteria: A healthy snapshot with only turnRecoveryBlockedUnsafe greater than zero remains healthy or OK in runtime, core health, the scheduled checker, fleet status, and console status.
The aggregate blocked count remains visible in an authorized diagnostic or operator projection without creating outage semantics.
Outstanding, exhausted, open-recovery, corrupt-link, and echo-conflict states retain their declared current-health effects.
A proof-promoted job moves from blocked audit evidence into the appropriate pending or outstanding current-state bucket exactly once.
Reassignment that preserves blocked-unsafe evidence does not manufacture a new health episode.
Repeated unchanged blocked counts do not re-page, refresh an outage, or require a restart to clear.
Any operator-attention episode has a distinct source, member identity, acknowledgement, disposition, and evidence-gated clear authority.
A deterministic guard fails when a numeric health field lacks a signal kind or consumers assign conflicting dispositions.
Exact-byte synthetic tests prove no routing identity, content, proof reference, location, process value, or private topology reaches public health or shared alerts.

falsifier_or_remaining_gap: The finding would be falsified if a healthy blocked-only snapshot remained OK through the scheduled checker while retaining its authorized diagnostic count. The exact-source canary instead produced checker_warn=true and runtime_agent_at_risk=true. Passing existing suites establish current behavior rather than the missing signal-kind contract; this review did not implement the cross-consumer matrix or observe production alert frequency.
impact: A safely retained replay refusal is presented as current runtime danger even though admission and later turns remain healthy. The warning can persist until administrative disposition, reducing trust in genuine recovery alerts and making evidence cleanup look like runtime healing.
